title: Unlocking Global Markets: Gabe Otte on the Future of Cross-Border Tokenization
ai_summary: Dinari's Gabe Otte discussed cross-border tokenization with Kakao Pay Securities, noting regulatory, not technological, hurdles. The goal is to turn home-market tokenized shares into compliant tokens for direct cross-border access. He sees potential for securities and commodities to follow stablecoin adoption.

title: Korea is Moving its Stocks Onchain, Here’s What it Means: Guest Post by ZyCrypto
ai_summary: Kakao Pay Securities announced a partnership with Ondo Finance and Dinari to develop a framework for listing Korean stocks in a global market. The firms will research underlying assets and token issuance this year. South Korea ranks 2nd globally in on-chain cryptocurrency holdings.

title: Dinari Expands Business Development Team to Scale Institutional Adoption of Tokenized Equities
ai_summary: Dinari appointed Umair Dandia, Vera Wang, and Isha Varshney to its business development team to scale institutional adoption of tokenized equities. The appointments target broker-dealers, asset managers, and decentralized markets, as the company provides over 700 tokenized U.S. stocks and ETFs. The team will expand integration across financial institutions and platforms.

title: tZERO Raises Funding Round
ai_summary: tZERO Group announced a new funding round led by Marc and Max Cohodes to support its blockchain-based infrastructure for tokenized financial markets. Existing investors ICE and Bill Fleckenstein, plus strategic partner Dinari, participated, with Neighborhood Intelligence to fund its portion upon a binding agreement. The company will use the capital for operations and to position itself for capital independence.

title: Dinari Powers Bitcoin.com’s U.S. Launch of Tokenized Equities
ai_summary: Dinari integrated its tokenized U.S. equities into Bitcoin.com, making them available to eligible U.S. users. The integration demonstrates a turnkey embedded model that can extend to broker-dealers and other financial platforms.

title: The AMC Fight Turned Into An Industry Argument Over Which Tokenized Stock Model Wins
ai_summary: A public debate over tokenized stock models emerged after AMC CEO Adam Aron clashed with Robinhood, with Dinari co-founder Gabriel Otte calling Robinhood and Ondo's tokens worse than common stocks. The three models compete for $2.91 billion, with Ondo leading at $869.6 million, and the SEC has mapped them into separate legal categories.
